**Dataset:** `campus_cafe_sales.csv` (posted with this assignment). 90 rows of daily sales for three campus cafés over six weekdays.




## Load

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px

sales = pd.read_csv("data/campus_cafe_sales.csv")
sales.head()
```

## Inspect

```{python}
print("Rows and columns:", sales.shape)
print("Cafes:", sales["cafe"].unique())
sales.dtypes
```

## Filter

```{python}
sales["revenue"] = sales["units_sold"] * sales["unit_price"]

coffee = sales[sales["category"] == "Coffee"]
coffee.head()
```

## Plot

```{python}
daily = coffee.groupby(["date", "cafe"], as_index=False)["revenue"].sum()

px.line(daily, x="date", y="revenue", color="cafe", markers=True,
        title="Daily coffee revenue by cafe",
        labels={"date": "Date", "revenue": "Revenue ($)"})
```

Three things worth knowing while you work:

- `"data/campus_cafe_sales.csv"` is a **relative path** — it is read from wherever `index.qmd` lives, not from wherever your terminal happens to be sitting. Keep it relative rather than pasting in a full `C:\Users\...` path, or the document will render on your machine and nowhere else.
- The last line of a chunk displays automatically — that is why `sales.head()` sits alone on its own line with no `print()` around it.
- `#| echo: false` at the top of a chunk hides the code but keeps the output. Use it on at least one chunk if you decide the reader wants the result and not the machinery.
